new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File checked. the PDF's metadata: Word-generated PDF dated 2021-06-08; running heads 'Linguistic Discovery 17.1:63-83 / Urban'; it is Urban 2021 'Cholón and the linguistic prehistory of northern Peru'. The quoted passage is on journal p.78 (between the '78' running head and the 'Urban 79' head; PDF p.16, confirmed with extracted text), in section 5 on areal typology, and matches the report verbatim including the bracketed ellipsis (the omitted text is 'So while final stress in Cholón chimes well with the fact that Den toponyms very frequently are stressed on the ending.. would seem a difficult task.' plus footnote call 28). Exact words: 'Tessmann's (1930: 458-459) Hibito data, on the other…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No stress rule can be stated for Hibito: the language is extinct and attested only by two short wordlists (43 + 33 items) plus a handful of remembered words; the only source that marks accent (Tessmann 1930) does so sporadically and shows both final and initial accents, so the position of word stress is undeterminable (unlike its sister Cholón, described as consistently final-stressed).
new_statements.exceptions: None; the author explicitly notes that not all of Tessmann's items carry a stress mark and that the marked ones disagree (final vs initial).
new_statements.domain_note: Observation concerns accent marks on isolated citation forms in a 1920s explorer's wordlist; no phonological analysis of Hibito exists (Urban 2021:69 'no grammar of the language survives'; Alexander-Bakkerus 2005:21-22).
new_statements.identity_note: Hibito proper (hibi1243, ISO hib), the extinct sister of Cholón (chol1284) in Hibito-Cholon (hibi1242). The quoted remark concerns Tessmann's 1920s Hibito wordlist; the same passage states that Cholón (not Hibito) had consistent final stress. Do not transfer the Cholón final-stress rule to Hibito.

sources.note: p.78: Cholón had consistent final stress (de la Mata, Poeppig, Tessmann), but Tessmann's (1930:458-459) Hibito data 'show an inconsistent pattern regarding stress' - not all items marked; of those marked, some final, some initial (<montsá>~<mantas> 'eye', <sótša> 'head'). Also p.69: no grammar of Hibito survives; documentation restricted to two wordlists.

sources.note: Phonology chapter is for Cholón only (final stress per de la Mata). On Hibito: pp.21-22 the only data are Martínez Compañón's 43-word list (1780s), Tessmann 1930:458-459 (33 words) and 4-5 words from a rememberer (Mrs. Gutiérrez, Juanjui 1996, App. 7.4.1, some with acute accents e.g. kóšwe, péyne, palánča); Araujo's 17th-c. Hibito grammar/vocabulary is untraceable. No statement about Hibito stress.
